title: Wave 54 Master Compendium (Attacks 225-228 / Discoveries 242-245 / Milestone Explorer v20.0): 100.0% Quires 1-4 (62/62 Extant Folios f1r-f32v), f12 Excised Stub Forensics on f13r, f15r/f15v Vellum-Hole Proof, Untranscribed f28v Flower-Center Micro-Inscription Discovery, and 204/227 (89.87%) Global Codex Visual Coverage

f12_excision_forensics.conjugate_partner: f13 (f13r/f13v) on innermost Bifolio 4 of Quire 2
f12_excision_forensics.foliation_chronology_proof: Folio numbers jump directly from '11' on f11r (p24) to '13' on f13r (p26), proving that leaf 12 was present when the 15th/16th-century foliator numbered the codex.
f12_excision_forensics.pigment_stub_on_f13r: At the left gutter margin of f13r (p26, x=0.00..0.03, y=0.24..0.38), the cut vellum stub of leaf f12 remains visible outside the sewing fold and preserves original crimson-brown and dark-green botanical pigment, proving f12 was a fully painted Herbal leaf prior to excision.

f15r_f15v_vellum_hole_proof.defect_type: Natural pre-existing vertical oval vellum hole (flaying defect / cicatrix)

f15r_recto_registration.botanical_integration: Illustrator positioned the central bifurcation fork of f15r's main stem directly around the oval vellum hole so the hole forms a hollow stem-node medallion at the exact junction of the two tall flower-pod stalks.
f15r_recto_registration.text_avoidance: Scribe 1 broke lines <f15r.12> (cth <-> cthol cthy) and <f15r.13> (qkol <-> dal dain) around the stem fork immediately above the hole.
f15r_recto_registration.show_through_folio: f16r (p32) — dark green digitate leaf tip of f16r is visible through the hole.

f15v_verso_registration.botanical_integration: Illustrator drew the upper-left broad leaf of the 4-leaved Paris quadrifolia whorl directly around the oval hole, leaving an unpainted white vellum reserve border around the rim.
f15v_verso_registration.show_through_folio: f14v (p29) — dark green serrated wing-leaf of f14v is visible through the hole.

opening_3quire_block.homogeneity: 46/46 extant folios (100.0%) written exclusively by Scribe 1 ($H=1) in Currier Language A ($L=A) before the first Scribe 2 / Currier B bifolium appears on f26r in Quire 4.

summary.palindromic_bifolio_structure: [Bif1 f25|f32: H1/A, Bif2 f26|f31: H2/B, Bif3 f27|f30: H1/A, Bif4 f28|f29: H1/A]

f28v_micro_inscription.location: Dead center of the unpainted white circular disc of the 18-rayed sunburst flower head (x=0.695..0.722, y=0.425..0.448)
f28v_micro_inscription.transliteration_status: COMPLETELY UNTRANSCRIBED in all 4 major EVA editions (ZL3b-n.txt, RF1b-er.txt, IT2a-n.txt, GC2a-n.txt record only the 9 paragraph lines <f28v.1..9> and 0 labels/notes)
f28v_micro_inscription.paleographic_reading: Three minute brown-ink characters ('iis' / 'w' / 'yir': two short vertical minims with top ticks and a sublinear hook followed by a taller hooked 's/r/v' sign), matching 15th-century workshop painter color-key annotations left visible because the central flower disc was never painted over.

companion_vellum_defects_on_leaf_28.hole_1_leaf_rosette: Natural vertical oval hole at f28r (x=0.66..0.69, y=0.46..0.51) inside the right blue-green leaf blade (exposing f29r) / f28v (x=0.34..0.38, y=0.45..0.52).
companion_vellum_defects_on_leaf_28.hole_2_stitched_double_hole: Original medieval stitched double vellum hole at f28r (x=0.18..0.29, y=0.64..0.75) / f28v (x=0.73..0.83, y=0.63..0.74, immediately below the right basal stem leaf, exposing f27v's green leaf).
